answer.content: The cluster holds one current deal, Granite Bay Building Supply, with no history deals; the deterministic engine fired only the deposit-pattern family (F5, weekday concentration 6.71 bits) and placed the hold because the STMT_TAMPER check failed on this deal's own documents (cluster_summary). Shared entities are mostly common in bank history—registered agent "lone star registered agents inc" (146 history deals), bank "frost hill bank" (66), phone "9725550123" (59), preparer "rosa benavides ea" (59), PDF producer "quickbooks online pdf" (18)—but the address "75217 9020 dallas june lake road tx" and guarantor "wade collins" each appear in 0 of 257 history deals (deal_entities; entity_deals). All seven application documents were produced by QuickBooks Online PDF and arrived within a 14-minute window on 2026-11-03, while bank statements came from FIS Statement Services 9.2 (deal_documents). A benign explanation I cannot rule out is that a small business legitimately uses a common registered agent, bank, preparer, and QuickBooks for document production, and a new address/guarantor is simply novel rather than fraudulent. However, the STMT_TAMPER failure on the bank statements and the unusual deposit pattern are not explained by those benign factors and warrant Fraud Operations review.
